title: ASME Audit Support in Tulsa | Air-Cooler & Exchanger NDE
description: Joint review prep for Tulsa air-cooler and heat exchanger shops: header NDE, Oklahoma rules, subcontractor control and a mock review. Talk to a Level III.
h1: ASME Joint Review Support in Tulsa: NDE Readiness for Heat Exchanger and Air-Cooler Builders
html:
Tulsa's Code shops build heat transfer equipment in volume: air-cooled exchangers for gas compression and processing, shell-and-tube bundles, and the header boxes and pressure parts that go into them. This page is for the quality manager or NDE lead at one of those shops who has an ASME joint review coming, either for a new certificate or for the three-year renewal. Atlantis NDT works from Houston and comes to your plant in Tulsa; an ASNT NDT Level III from Atlantis checks and prepares the nondestructive examination part of your quality control system so the review team finds a program that works. Send us your review date to start.

Tulsa's heat transfer manufacturing base

Air-cooled heat exchanger manufacturing has deep roots in Tulsa. One Tulsa-based air-cooler builder, Air-X-Changers (then part of Harsco and operating with Hammco), reported in 2017 that it had shipped its 100,000th ASME-certified cooler section and that it had received its first ASME Certificate of Authorization in 1957. That one example says a lot about the local pattern: certificate holders with production lines, repeat designs and decades of joint reviews behind them. Around the large builders sit smaller exchanger and vessel fabricators, tube-bundle and header specialists, and heavy fabricators near the Port of Catoosa at the head of the Arkansas River navigation channel, where Tulsa-headquartered Matrix Service lists a fabrication facility.

The customers are the gas compression packagers, midstream processors, refineries, petrochemical plants and power stations of Oklahoma, Texas and beyond. Cooler sections built in Tulsa end up on compressor skids in the Permian Basin, at gas plants across the Mid-Continent and in Canada. That geography shapes the NDE program, because the same production line has to satisfy many purchasers' specifications and many jurisdictions at once.

What header-box production asks of your NDE program

An air-cooler section is mostly tubes, fins and structure, but the pressure boundary that the joint review cares about is concentrated in the headers. Rectangular plug-type and cover-plate headers are designed under Section VIII Division 1's rules for vessels of noncircular cross section. Their corner and tee joints between tubesheet, plugsheet, top and bottom plates and end plates are awkward to radiograph, which pushes more of the volumetric work toward ultrasonic examination wherever the design and the Code allow it. Nozzle welds, pass partition welds and any tube-to-tubesheet welds add surface examinations to the mix.

Production volume changes how NDE should be documented. Rather than a procedure rewritten for every job, a Tulsa shop needs a controlled set of procedures plus technique sheets for each header design family, approved under the written practice and reissued when a design changes. The review team will pick a header off the floor or out of the records and ask which technique sheet covered each weld, who approved that sheet, and whether the examiner was certified for the method on that date. A technique sheet that still shows a plate thickness the shop stopped buying two years ago is the kind of detail they notice.

Joint efficiency drives a second set of questions. Whether a seam is fully radiographed, spot radiographed or not radiographed at all follows from the design calculation, and under spot radiography Division 1 gives the Inspector a say in where the spots go. Your travelers should carry the examination extent from the design to the floor, and your records should show who selected each spot and when. For the Code background, see our pages on Section VIII Division 1 and Section V Article 4.

Shell-and-tube exchangers and the tube-to-tubesheet question

Tulsa's shell-and-tube builders face a different mix. Shell and channel seams, nozzle welds and flange attachments follow the familiar Division 1 examination rules, but tube-to-tubesheet joints are where shop practice varies most. Many are expanded only, some are seal-welded, and some are strength-welded to carry load. Each choice brings its own examination and testing expectations, and purchasers in refining and petrochemical service often add penetrant examination of tube-to-tubesheet welds and specific leak testing on top of the Code. The review team will not redesign your joints, but it will check that the examination you claim on the traveler matches the joint type on the drawing and that a qualified person performed it to an accepted procedure.

Penetrant work on these joints deserves care. The procedure has to address surface preparation on tight, curved weld faces, dwell time, excess penetrant removal without over-washing, developer application and lighting, and the materials themselves need contaminant control where the tubesheet or tubes are austenitic stainless steel or nickel alloy. Our page on Section V Article 6 summarizes the requirements that the procedure should carry.

Oklahoma's boiler and pressure vessel program

Oklahoma regulates more than boilers. The Boiler and Pressure Vessel Service within the Oklahoma Department of Labor's Safety Standards Division has jurisdiction over high-pressure boilers, low-pressure steam and hot water boilers and other pressure vessels, and it licenses the firms that install, service and repair them. A permit is required before installation, inspectors must hold a National Board commission, and the division registers and inspects the equipment: boilers at least once a year, high-pressure boilers twice, and some pressure vessels every three years. Oklahoma is a National Board member jurisdiction.

For a Tulsa manufacturer, the practical effect is twofold. Equipment installed in Oklahoma, and repairs done in Oklahoma, fall under that program, so a shop with a field repair arm needs its state licensing in order alongside any National Board R certificate. And because much of what Tulsa builds ships elsewhere, the Manufacturer's Data Report and National Board registration have to satisfy the jurisdiction at the destination as well. Canadian shipments add a Canadian Registration Number for the design. None of that changes the Code's NDE rules, but it multiplies the purchaser and jurisdiction extras that your travelers must capture without error.

Where Tulsa shops put their NDE people

Long-established certificate holders in Tulsa often run their own NDE departments, with Level II personnel for visual, penetrant and magnetic particle work and, at the larger plants, ultrasonic technicians on staff. Some employ a Level III; many rely on an outside one for the written practice, examinations and procedure approval. Radiography is usually brought in from a licensed radiography company, sometimes working in a shielded bay on the manufacturer's premises, because licensing and exposure control are specialized.

The risk in a long-running program is drift rather than absence. The written practice was written years ago and still cites an older SNT-TC-1A edition. The Level III who wrote it has retired, and nobody has re-approved the procedures since. Qualification examinations were given by a supervisor who no longer qualifies to give them. Experience hours were never written down because everyone knew the technicians had them. These are the findings our NDT audit consulting work turns up most often in mature shops, and they are the ones a renewal team can sample quickly.

Renewal reviews for long-established certificate holders

Every three years the certificate comes up for renewal, and ASME asks the applicant to give the team leader a list of all Code work performed in the shop and at field sites since the last joint review, with the records of that work available. For a high-volume air-cooler plant that list is long, and the team samples it. The real test of your NDE program is whether any job on the list can be opened and traced in a few minutes: the technique sheet, the examination report, the images or data, the examiner's certification valid on the date, the calibration of the instrument used, and the acceptance signature.

Shops that keep NDE records in a mix of paper travelers, a lab's emailed PDFs and a spreadsheet of certification dates struggle with that test even when the work itself was sound. If that describes you, our page on the audit evidence scramble shows how to put examination records, certificates and calibrations behind one search, and the equipment calibration page covers instruments that drift past their due date.

Subcontracted radiography and the paper that proves control

Whoever exposes the film, the certificate holder answers for it. Here is what a Tulsa shop's file on its radiography company should hold, and why each item matters to the team:

DocumentWhy the team asks for itGap we often see
The radiography company's written practiceShows how its technicians are trained, examined and certifiedCopy on file is two revisions old
Radiography procedure accepted for your workSection V requires a written procedure meeting Article 2No record of who on your side accepted it
Technician certifications and vision recordsThe examiner must be qualified on the day of the exposureVision examination expired mid-job
Technique details per header familyGeometry and thickness change between designsSame technique used for every header thickness
Your review of the radiographsYour organization accepts the images before the Inspector doesLab's interpretation accepted with no shop signature

Atlantis reviews these documents as an independent Level III. We expose no film in the US, which keeps that review clean. The same discipline applies to UT contractors; our subcontractor approval audit page describes the full method.

What Atlantis does in Tulsa and what stays with you

Our work on a Tulsa joint review covers the NDE thread through your system. We read the written practice against the SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 edition your Code references and rewrite it where needed through our written practice development service. We check the procedures and the technique sheets for each header family against Section V and the construction Code, and write replacements under procedure development. We audit each examiner's file for training hours, experience, examination grades and vision, prepare qualification demonstrations where they are required, and draft the NDE wording of the subcontracting and records sections of your manual. Then we run a mock review of the NDE portion on your floor, pulling real jobs from the list of Code work the way the team will.

The certificate stays yours, along with its obligations. Your Authorized Inspection Agency accepts the manual and its Inspector signs the data reports; ASME decides on the certificate after the team recommends. Atlantis holds none of those roles. The welding program, with its procedure specifications, qualification records and welder qualifications, belongs to your welding engineer; Atlantis does not author or qualify welding procedures, and the WPS, PQR and WPQ guide explains that side. Nuclear certificates under Section III are not part of what we support.

Tulsa audit-readiness checklist

  1. List every header design family in production and confirm each has a current, approved technique sheet for each method applied to it.
  2. Check that design joint efficiencies and examination extents appear on the traveler for each job, not just in the calculation.
  3. For spot radiography, confirm the records show who chose each spot location and when.
  4. Re-read the written practice: Code edition, SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 edition, Level III named, examination and recertification rules.
  5. Audit every examiner file for training hours, experience hours by method, examination results and the date of the last vision examination.
  6. Pull the calibration history for UT instruments and reference blocks, MT yokes, light meters and penetrant material batch certifications.
  7. Assemble the radiography company file described above and add the same for any UT contractor.
  8. Prepare the list of all Code work since the last review and test whether five random entries can be traced in minutes.
  9. If you run a field repair crew, confirm Oklahoma licensing and the R certificate, and see the NBIC R-stamp NDT audit support page.
  10. Walk the people the team will interview through the questions they are likely to hear.

How an engagement runs

Start by sending the designators and scope on your certificate, the expected review month, the NDE-related sections of your quality control manual, your written practice, your procedure and technique sheet index, and the names of your NDE subcontractors. We review remotely and send back a gap list with each item tied to a manual paragraph and a Code requirement, sorted by how long it takes to close. A site visit follows: record sampling, floor walk, examiner interviews and a mock review of the NDE portion. After that we stay on call while your team closes items, and we reply within one business day.

Shops that want an outside Level III on an ongoing basis can read about Level III of record in Tulsa; for refinery-side work in the region, refining NDT consulting in Tulsa; and for the city overview, NDT consulting in Tulsa. Technicians who need formal training can take our SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training for Tulsa, after which your company certifies them. The full service description is on the national ASME audit Level III support page, and Gulf Coast suppliers can compare our Houston ASME audit support notes.

faq.q: Our air-cooler headers are rectangular. Does that change the NDE the team looks at?
faq.a: It changes which examinations are practical. Corner and tee joints on noncircular headers are hard to radiograph, so ultrasonic and surface examinations carry more weight, and the team will check that each joint's examination is defined on an approved technique sheet.

faq.q: We have held our certificate for decades. What does a renewal team look at on the NDE side?
faq.a: It samples the list of Code work since the last review and traces NDE records on those jobs: technique, report, images or data, examiner certification on the date, instrument calibration and acceptance. Long-running programs are usually caught on drift, such as an outdated written practice or undocumented experience hours.

faq.q: Does Oklahoma regulate pressure vessels as well as boilers?
faq.a: Yes. The Oklahoma Department of Labor's Boiler and Pressure Vessel Service covers boilers and other pressure vessels, requires a permit before installation and licenses firms that install, service and repair them.

faq.q: Who should approve our technique sheets?
faq.a: Your written practice should say. In most SNT-TC-1A programs a Level III approves procedures and the techniques that implement them. If your Level III has left, see Level III of record in Tulsa.

faq.q: Our UT technicians were certified in-house years ago. Will the team check how?
faq.a: Expect it. The team or the Authorized Inspector may ask for the certification record behind a technician's name: training hours, experience, general, specific and practical examination results, and vision. Our experience log page explains how to rebuild missing evidence honestly.

faq.q: Can Atlantis perform the UT on our headers and also run the mock review?
faq.a: Atlantis technicians can carry out ultrasonic, magnetic particle, penetrant and visual examinations in your plant, but we advise against using the same person to examine welds and then audit that work. If we inspect for you, a different Level III reviews the program, or we keep the two jobs separate.

faq.q: We ship cooler sections to Canada. Does that affect the NDE file?
faq.a: The Code's NDE rules stay the same, but provincial registration of the design and purchaser specifications often add requirements. Your traveler should show any extra examination so the record proves it was done.

faq.q: Can you help our repair department prepare for its R certificate review?
faq.a: Yes, on the NDE portion. Our NBIC R-stamp NDT audit support page explains what the National Board review checks.

faq.q: Is nuclear Section III work included?
faq.a: No. Section III nuclear certificates are outside what Atlantis supports.
